title: Trách nhiệm cá nhân và điều trị · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support charging higher public healthcare fees to people whose illnesses are linked to lifestyle choices, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

outline.purpose: Giải thích vì sao người ủng hộ tin cơ chế có ích và vì sao bên phản đối thấy chi phí đáng lo; sau đó nêu lựa chọn riêng. Nêu hạn chế của chính sách chưa tự động giải thích được lý do phản đối. Không dùng “lifestyle choices” như bằng chứng mọi bệnh đều do lỗi cá nhân. Thu nhập, môi trường sống và nghiện giới hạn lựa chọn; còn khó xác định bao nhiêu phần bệnh do hành vi.
outline.content: Higher treatment charges assume that responsibility for illness can be separated neatly from addiction and living conditions. I oppose higher public treatment fees for lifestyle-related illness because they can deter care without giving disadvantaged patients a realistic way to change.

outline.purpose: Phí cao làm hậu quả tài chính rõ hơn, có thể thay động cơ một số người. Ví dụ người hút thuốc chỉ hợp lý khi hỗ trợ cai nghiện dễ tiếp cận; nghiện không phải lựa chọn có thể đảo ngay bằng ý chí.
outline.content: Supporters argue that personal contributions may encourage some people to consider preventable health risks.

paragraphs: Higher treatment charges assume that responsibility for illness can be separated neatly from addiction and living conditions. I oppose higher public treatment fees for lifestyle-related illness because they can deter care without giving disadvantaged patients a realistic way to change.

Supporters argue that personal contributions may encourage some people to consider preventable health risks. A visible financial consequence can make the costs of repeated harmful behaviour harder to ignore. A smoker offered accessible cessation support might reconsider a costly habit. That incentive is most plausible where cessation support makes change achievable; a financial threat alone may have limited force against dependency or constrained living conditions. Charging more may discourage timely treatment among people with the fewest resources, even when their illness is partly associated with behaviour.

Opponents warn that lifestyle is shaped by income, addiction and living conditions, so charging can punish disadvantage. Additional charges can make people postpone appointments rather than change an addictive behaviour. Illness may then become more serious and costly to treat, while clinicians face the difficult task of separating personal choice from income, environment and other causes. Public treatment should remain accessible while prevention addresses the conditions behind harmful choices. Keeping treatment accessible avoids punishing delayed presentation, while support for prevention can address risk without requiring clinicians to assign a simplistic share of personal blame. I would favour accessible prevention over punitive treatment fees, because accountability must be balanced against addiction, constrained choices and the consequences of delayed care. A possible incentive to quit is outweighed by delayed care and the difficulty of assigning personal blame for illnesses with several interacting causes.
Accessible treatment and practical prevention offer a fairer response than punitive fees, which can make illness worse precisely among patients least able to afford timely help.

Giả định tăng phí luôn khiến người nghiện đổi hành vi thay vì bỏ khám.
Bỏ qua khó khăn khi xác định tỷ lệ bệnh do lối sống.
review: Task Response: Kết luận trả lại cả hai cách nhìn và quyết định của người viết; không cần chia đều số câu nhưng phải giải thích thực chất cả hai phía. Đã xử lý phản biện “Lifestyle is shaped by income, addiction and living conditions, so charging can punish disadvantage.” chưa?
